Honestly, this place looks like the perfect setting for someone to dance with the devil.

On Wednesday's episode of "The Daily Show," host Josh Johnson pointed out a detail from Donald Trump Jr.'s wedding that looks like it could have come straight out of a hit horror movie—and once you see it, you can't unsee it.

Johnson first played a clip of Trump sharing footage from his wedding to socialite Bettina Trump (held in May on a small island in the Bahamas), then delivered his punchline.

The footage, set to an acoustic version of The Ronettes' classic "Be My Baby," features an aerial shot of the church where the president's eldest son got married, followed by interior shots of the guests. Trump's daughters Ivanka and Tiffany Trump can be seen sitting in the pews, followed by slow-motion footage of the bride and groom embracing at the altar beneath a giant cross.

Johnson quipped: "A beautiful ceremony held in the church from 'Sinners,'" showing a still from the Oscar-winning film of Sammie (played by Miles Caton) walking into his father's church covered in blood. Above Sammie, just like above Trump Jr. and his bride, hangs a massive cross. The exterior of the church in "Sinners" also looks remarkably similar to the one in the Bahamas.

The wedding has come under intense scrutiny after ProPublica reported earlier this week that Trump Jr.'s nuptials were bankrolled by Russian oligarch Umar Kremlev, who has close ties to Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Responding to the controversy, Bettina Trump released a statement on Instagram clarifying: "Don and I were married privately last Friday, surrounded by just our family."

She continued: "The weekend that followed had been planned long before, as a weekend with friends. It was never intended to be our wedding weekend. When our original wedding plans changed, we simply decided to get married beforehand and attend the already-scheduled weekend as a newlywed couple."

She also wrote that the couple's "friend Umar was incredibly generous and hosted two wonderful celebratory evenings for us after our wedding."

Johnson also had a devastating response to Bettina Trump's clarification.

Johnson, imitating Bettina Trump's tone, said: "Yes, that's right, it's fake news. They didn't pay for my wedding—they paid for a much fancier after-party."
